candidate.answerReason: For a one-way distance of \(d>0\) miles, total distance is \(2d\) and total time is \(5d/2\) minutes. Their quotient is \(4/5\) mile per minute, or \(48\) miles per hour.

methods.label: Combine the distances and times
methods.explanation:
Average speed is total distance divided by total time. Let \(d>0\) be the one-way distance measured in miles; its numerical value will cancel.

The outward pace is \(2\) minutes per mile, so that leg takes \(2d\) minutes. The return speed is \(2\) miles per minute, so the return takes \(d/2\) minutes. Hence
\[
\text{total distance}=2d\text{ miles},
\qquad
\text{total time}=2d+\frac d2=\frac{5d}{2}\text{ minutes}.
\]
Because \(d>0\), we may cancel it in the quotient:
\[
\text{average speed}
=\frac{2d}{5d/2}
=\frac45\text{ mile per minute}.
\]
There are \(60\) minutes in an hour, giving
\[
\frac45\cdot60=48\text{ miles per hour}.
\]
Thus the answer is choice B, independently of the value of \(m\).
